Thal 0: Cells from an aged human brain with no amyloid-beta deposition: no detectable amyloid plaques in any brain region.
Thal 1: Cells from a human brain with the earliest phase of amyloid-beta deposition: plaques restricted to the neocortex, with subcortical regions unaffected.
Thal 2: Cells from a human brain with early amyloid-beta spread: neocortical plaques plus involvement of allocortical regions including entorhinal cortex and hippocampus.
Thal 3: Cells from a human brain with intermediate amyloid-beta spread: plaques extending into deep subcortical nuclei including basal ganglia and thalamus.
Thal 4: Cells from a human brain with advanced amyloid-beta spread: plaque deposition reaching brainstem structures in addition to cortical and subcortical involvement.
Thal 5: Cells from a human brain with the final phase of amyloid-beta spread: diffuse plaque deposition throughout the neuraxis including cerebellum, with global amyloid burden.
nan: Cells from a human brain with uncharacterized neuropathology.
